title: Namespaces, cgroups and union filesystems — the general idea

videos.script: Lesson one called a container a process with walls. This lesson takes the walls apart. There are three pieces, and the kernel already had all of them before Docker existed. {{namespaces}} Namespaces decide what a process can see. You will read them straight out of slash proc, and step through one with nsenter. {{cgroups}} Control groups decide how much it can use. The limits are plain files. You will read them, and then hit them. A loop that forks stops at twenty processes. A loop that eats memory is killed, with exit code one hundred and thirty seven. {{overlay}} And overlayfs builds the files. The image's layers sit at the bottom, read-only. One empty layer on top takes every write. A deleted file leaves a strange little marker behind. By the end you will know where every byte of a container lives.
